body:
### Summary

This PR fixes several problems in how ClimaLand partitions radiation, momentum, heat, and water between the canopy and the ground, and in the turbulent exchange with the atmosphere under stable and calm conditions. The problems were found by comparing global runs (ERA5, CLASS, FLUXCOM) and FLUXNET sites against the model after the prognostic skin temperature solve (#1894):

- At night under stable stratification, uncapped Monin–Obukhov exchange collapsed and canopies and snow decoupled from the ground and cooled away from the atmosphere (canopy up to 6 K colder than the air).
- The canopy displacement height coefficient (0.0416) dated from when canopy height was fixed at 1 m; at tall forest sites, it overestimated the effective measurement height by up to 2.3x and underestimated friction velocity.
- Canopy radiation, longwave emissivity, heat capacity, and sensible heat exchange used LAI alone, ignoring stems (SAI). Leafless or sparse canopies let too much radiation through and were thermally decoupled.
- Farquhar capacities were scaled linearly by LAI, without the cap arising from the vertical decline of leaf nitrogen, thus overestimating assimilation in dense canopies.
- The ground below a canopy was driven by the above-canopy wind, temperature, and humidity. This produced more soil evaporation than transpiration in temperate forests and globally, and no sheltering under short canopies. Water vapor could also "transpire" backwards into leaves when the air was more humid than the leaf.
- The P-model applied soil moisture stress only through a 36-day acclimation average, so stomata reacted to drought and rewetting weeks late. `PiecewiseMoistureStressModel` used porosity instead of field capacity as its wet threshold, which stressed even wet soils (global mean βm = 0.53).
- The wind in the flux solves was floored at a constant 1 m/s; in calm convective conditions, this let skin temperatures run away.
- There were no 2 m temperature/humidity or 10 m wind diagnostics.

### Commits

Each commit loads and passes its tests on its own.

1. [`07f343fbc`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/07f343fbc38d0f6b2a030ac0700d54d1a4beaa52) **Stability cap.** All land surface flux solves use `SurfaceFluxes.MaxHeatFluxStabilityCap`, which holds the exchange coefficients at the stability of maximum downward heat flux (parameter-free; capped u* is about 2/3 of neutral, consistent with observed nighttime/neutral u*/U ratios of 0.65–0.79 at four FLUXNET sites). SurfaceFluxes compat raised to 1.3. New `test/shared_utilities/stability_cap.jl`.
2. [`574620f54`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/574620f5445bd0329a6f41f770a564217ffffc0d) **Displacement height.** `canopy_d_coeff = 0.67` (Brutsaert 1982; Raupach 1994) in both TOML files; documents `canopy_z_0m_coeff`, `canopy_z_0b_coeff`, `canopy_d_coeff`, `leaf_Cd`.
3. [`39b07bf98`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/39b07bf98ac10f974b42b7a03a6eabb102f549f1) **FLUXNET setup and soil fixes.** Updates `p.soil.θ_l` in `make_update_implicit_aux`; masks frozen-soil moisture sensor readings when initializing soil water and bounds the initial soil water below at the wilting point (observed water contents below θ_r of the gridded parameters produced NaNs at US-SRG after the first rain); converts `soil_vg_α` at US-NR1/US-MOz/US-Ha1 from cm⁻¹ to m⁻¹ and aligns `K_sat_plant` with the default TOML; adds `soilrn`, `soilshf`, `soillhf` diagnostics.
4. [`8e4cd4a10`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/8e4cd4a101501303c9d1ea665f75dfad790e8825) **Plant area index.** Uses LAI + SAI (with plant-area-weighted leaf/stem optics) in two-stream and Beer–Lambert radiative transfer, longwave emissivity, canopy heat capacity, and canopy sensible heat conductance; photosynthesis and SIF use the leaf share of absorbed PAR. Farquhar capacities are scaled by the canopy-mean nitrogen factor (1 − exp(−k_n LAI))/(k_n LAI), k_n = 0.5 (Sellers et al. 1992).
5. [`dfe0e3d30`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/dfe0e3d30a9af4633899b526da06dd77084c8bc1) **Moisture stress.** P-model acclimates well-watered capacities and applies βm instantaneously to GPP, Rd, An, and gs (Stocker et al. 2020). `PiecewiseMoistureStressModel` uses the van Genuchten field capacity θ_fc = θ_r + S_c(ν − θ_r) as its upper threshold when the retention model is available (Lehmann et al. 2008; Assouline & Or 2014).
6. [`532a7b171`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/532a7b171c59e870461c8c8a75e1acf9eebe9736) **Audit fixes.** Documents the frozen-soil vapor weight and the `lhf` sign convention, fixes the `heaviside` docstring, removes a dead return in `compute_ρ_sfc`. Adds the restart-reproducible initial-guess norm to `AGENTS.md`.
7. [`19b618ae7`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/19b618ae75fba400ba895aa4297b046ed9818312) **Screen-level diagnostics.** `t2m`, `q2m`, `u10m` reconstructed from the Monin–Obukhov profiles of the soil, snow, canopy, and integrated flux solves.
8. [`cf65b20b5`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/cf65b20b57ff4879b17852cd6613998f3952b7ea) **Ground below a canopy.** The soil and snow under a canopy exchange with the canopy air at height d + z_0m (floored at `canopy_subcanopy_min_reference_height`, 2 m), with the wind attenuated by exp(−α PAI) (`canopy_subcanopy_wind_extinction_coefficient`, 0.5; Inoue 1963; Cionco 1965), and with the canopy-air temperature and humidity from the canopy flux solve where LAI + SAI ≥ 0.05 (Shuttleworth & Wallace 1985). Bare ground recovers the forcing. The flux functions take `h_atmos`, `u_atmos`, `T_atmos`, `q_atmos`, `gustiness` keywords; canopy fluxes are evaluated before the ground skin solve so restarts stay bit-for-bit. Canopy humidity is floored at the air humidity and canopy LHF is zeroed where the vapor flux would be negative. Tests in `test_canopy_helpers.jl`.
9. [`c651e02a1`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/c651e02a1c5b4e084ed44a34bd7f68942eaf98b9) **Convective gustiness.** `FlooredDeardorffGustiness`: the larger of a constant floor and the Deardorff velocity β(B z_i)^{1/3} (Beljaars 1995), evaluated in closed form inside the SurfaceFluxes solve so it stays non-iterative and restart-reproducible. Default `FlooredDeardorffGustiness(1 m/s)` for `PrescribedAtmosphere` and the forcing helpers; a plain number keeps the constant floor. Below a canopy, the floor is folded into the sub-canopy wind and the ground keeps the convective part.
10. [`3e8cd3049`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/3e8cd30491742fc8399c7a7e76a1b9486d777195) **SurfaceFluxes 1.5.** The surface state of a flux solve applies at the displacement height: the sensible heat flux is driven by c_p (T_air − T_sfc) + g (Δz − d), and the surface air density is extrapolated over Δz − d, in SurfaceFluxes and in the land code that reproduces parts of the solve (canopy energy balance, skin-temperature callbacks, flux derivatives, and the screen-level reconstruction, which delegates to `SurfaceFluxes.screen_level_values`). The gustiness floor accessors of SurfaceFluxes replace the land versions. `AtmosDrivenCanopyBC` checks that the forcing height exceeds d + max(z_0m, z_0b), below which SurfaceFluxes returns NaN. The screen-level means count the canopy only where plants are present. SurfaceFluxes compat 1.5; ClimaParams compat 1.3.1.
11. [`ab8e8d799`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/commit/ab8e8d79928052c13c13036fb53c7002eead7a1f) **CI caches.** The cached depots of the CI, docs, downgrade, and downstream workflows fall back only to a depot of the same Julia version. The downstream ClimaCoupler commands run without color output, since precompiling the standard libraries at -O0 into an empty depot overflowed the stack in Julia 1.12's colored output.

### Results

**Stability cap and displacement height (4 FLUXNET sites, P-model)**

- US-Ha1 (h_c = 26 m): u* RMSE 0.38 (uncapped) → 0.28 (cap) → 0.15 m/s (d = 0.67 h_c), r 0.73 → 0.91; nighttime u* 0.09 → 0.41 m/s (obs 0.46); nighttime H −3.2 → −28.4 W/m² (obs −30.3).
- US-NR1 (h_c = 14 m): LW↑ RMSE 29.5 → 16.2 → 14.1 W/m² (r 0.98); u* RMSE 0.28 → 0.16 m/s.
- US-MOz (h_c = 18.5 m): LW↑ RMSE 22.8 → 16.3 W/m² (r 0.99); u* RMSE 0.14 m/s.

**Canopy–ground partitioning (4 FLUXNET sites, commits 3–5)**

- Daytime (SW↓ > 50 W/m²): US-NR1 soil Rn 193 → 65 W/m², soil H 109 → −6, canopy H 85 → 142 (total H 137 vs obs 136). US-MOz soil Rn 131 → 85, soil LE 87 → 36–40, total H 1 → 94–110 (obs 106).
- Half-hourly RMSE (W/m²; raw / energy-balance-corrected fluxes; GPP in µmol/m²/s):

| Site | Config | H RMSE (raw / corr) | LE RMSE (raw / corr) | LE r | GPP bias / RMSE / r |
| :-- | :-- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| US-NR1 | Farquhar | 71.9 → 69.0 / 85.1 → 84.7 | 53.5 → 51.9 / 60.6 → 58.7 | 0.69 → 0.71 | +0.16 / 2.70 / 0.79 |
| US-NR1 | P-model | 75.0 → 69.1 / 78.1 → 77.3 | 52.6 → 47.8 / 68.4 → 62.3 | 0.61 → 0.69 | +0.11 / 1.56 / 0.93 (was −0.76 / 2.18) |
| US-MOz | Farquhar | 80.8 → 74.3 / 98.5 → 94.4 | 73.3 → 68.9 / 101.1 → 96.1 | 0.77 → 0.80 | +1.00 / 4.87 / 0.79 |
| US-MOz | P-model | 92.9 → 77.6 / 93.0 → 82.7 | 53.5 → 42.0 / 110.1 → 95.0 | 0.88 → 0.92 | +0.18 / 2.64 / 0.92 (was −1.30 / 3.94) |
| US-Ha1 | Farquhar | 77.4 → 72.3 / — | 70.8 → 64.5 / — | 0.83 → 0.86 | +2.34 / 6.40 / 0.87 |
| US-Ha1 | P-model | 71.3 → 64.2 / — | 72.3 → 67.4 / — | 0.90 → 0.91 | −0.43 / 4.16 / 0.92 (was −1.76 / 5.64) |
| US-Var | Farquhar | 39.6 → 34.6 / 34.8 → 34.1 | 26.8 → 24.1 / 28.2 → 25.1 | 0.92 → 0.94 | −0.34 / 3.16 / 0.79 |

**FLUXNET2015, 38 sites, `main` → PR (full branch)**

365-day runs after 30 days of spin-up; half-hourly fluxes with QC = 0, uncorrected tower H/LE; tower-pixel MODIS LAI and IGBP leaf optics on both branches; P-model. `main` produced NaNs at US-SRG and US-Whs and did not finish US-Wkg; the PR runs all 38. The 35 sites that finish on both are compared (site-mean statistics, W/m²):

| | All (35) | Forest (17) | Non-forest (18) |
| :-- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| LE bias | +10.3 → +5.1 | +5.4 → +1.2 | +15.0 → +8.8 |
| LE \|bias\| | 15.6 → 14.9 | 12.0 → 15.7 | 18.9 → 14.2 |
| LE RMSE | 49.8 → 46.9 | 50.2 → 51.3 | 49.4 → 42.7 |
| LE r | 0.81 → 0.81 | 0.81 → 0.80 | 0.81 → 0.82 |
| H bias | +5.5 → +8.0 | +6.9 → +6.2 | +4.2 → +9.6 |
| H RMSE | 57.2 → 58.8 | 66.5 → 67.6 | 48.5 → 50.6 |
| H r | 0.84 → 0.87 | 0.85 → 0.89 | 0.83 → 0.84 |
| LW↑ RMSE | 17.5 → 13.8 | 21.0 → 10.9 | 15.2 → 15.7 |
| LW↑ night \|bias\| | 9.2 → 4.4 | 16.4 → 3.5 | 4.4 → 5.0 |
| SW↑ RMSE | 27.3 → 26.8 | 24.9 → 19.3 | 29.3 → 33.0 |
| Rn RMSE | 39.0 → 37.1 | 45.6 → 38.9 | 33.1 → 35.5 |

- LE RMSE improves at 17 sites and worsens at 8; H RMSE improves at 18 and worsens at 15; LE+H RMSE improves at 20 of 35 sites.
- Forests: most of the nighttime longwave error is gone (LW↑ RMSE 21 → 11, night |bias| 16.4 → 3.5), SW↑ and Rn improve, H correlation rises. E.g. US-MMS LE RMSE 71 → 55, DE-Tha H RMSE 53 → 42, US-GLE H RMSE 103 → 82, IT-Cp2 LE/H RMSE 54/79 → 46/70.
- Non-forest: the excess floor evaporation under short canopies is removed: AT-Neu LE RMSE 75 → 37, CH-Cha 50 → 39, DE-Gri 46 → 30, US-Los 62 → 44, US-Ne1 94 → 73; US-ARM H RMSE 71 → 64, FR-Gri 42 → 35.
- Regressions: at wet grasslands (AT-Neu, CH-Cha, DE-Gri, US-Los) and US-Syv the H bias rises to +20–30 W/m² because transpiration does not replace the removed floor evaporation and SW↑ is too low there. At tropical/broadleaf forests LE becomes too low (BR-Sa1 LE RMSE 50 → 68, H 56 → 91; GF-Guy 70 → 87, 58 → 81; DK-Sor LE 42 → 53): the previous excess soil evaporation was masking under-transpiring broadleaf canopies. US-Prr trades LE (17 → 31) for H (50 → 32). These are canopy-side problems (conductance calibration, a litter layer for nighttime floor evaporation) and will be addressed in a follow-up PR.

**Global runs**

- 2-year 180×360×15 GPU run, year 2, `main` → commit 4: LW↑ vs ERA5 bias −6.45 → −3.57 W/m², annual RMSE 28.6 → 27.3; SW↑ vs ERA5 bias +0.69 → −0.07; LE annual RMSE 19.0 → 18.2 (ERA5) and 21.2 → 19.4 (CLASS).
- 1-year 45×24×15 GPU run, commit 4 → sub-canopy wind + instantaneous βm + field capacity: LE vs CLASS bias +9.96 → +8.63, annual RMSE 16.6 → 15.4, monthly 27.7 → 26.4; LE vs FLUXCOM boreal bias +2.37 → +0.30, annual RMSE 7.7 → 6.0; H vs ERA5 bias −1.39 → −0.47, annual RMSE 17.2 → 16.3, monthly 29.6 → 28.3; H annual/monthly RMSE 16.1/26.5 → 15.6/25.5 (CLASS), 22.8/32.2 → 21.8/30.8 (FLUXCOM).
- Sub-canopy soil evaporation 26.7 → 23.4 W/m² globally (Amazon 36.8 → 27.3, Europe 40.6 → 29.8); T/ET 0.41 → 0.47 globally (Amazon 0.62 → 0.71, East US 0.39 → 0.49, Europe 0.24 → 0.34 with H −10.6 → −1.6 W/m² vs ERA5 +12.1).

title: ## Improve Land Surface Energy Fluxes and Canopy–Ground Partitioning
